summary: noxleys 1.1.0: static patterns match on Baileys-family WhatsApp library; installer-harm not corroborated
details: Package appears to be a WhatsApp Web (Baileys-family) client library. a static rule fired on lib/Utils/messages-media.js for co-occurrence of require('child_process'), require('os'), require('http')/require('https'), Buffer.from base64 decoding, and POST/fetch calls, alongside a hardcoded https://mmg.whatsapp.net endpoint (WhatsApp's own media server used by all Baileys forks for legitimate media upload/download). Buffer.from usage in chat-utils.js and messages-media.js is consistent with protocol message framing and media (de)ciphering. The flagged shape — child_process + os + http + base64 + POST — is the normal composition of a WhatsApp media client and does not by itself demonstrate exfiltration of installer secrets, install-time execution of remote code, or a hardcoded attacker C2. Semantic verification of the traced code paths was not completed here, so a specific covert side-effect (e.g., an undocumented auto-follow, install counter, or hidden relay bolted onto the Baileys API) cannot be confirmed or ruled out from the available signals.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
